findings.summary: The doc update would extend a claim the code does not enforce for code-check and design-change.
findings.evidence: Line 382 already says code-check and design-change cases "do not become candidates". But read_records (introspect.rs:392-412) pushes every Recorded introspection that has a class into cases, whatever its kind, and the earlier grep found no prevention_kind reader in proposals.rs. The plan's wording is "relax and remove join code-check and design-change ... backed by the read_records filter". That filter covers only relax and remove. Fix: Say that the read_records filter enforces the rule for relax and remove only. Do not attribute the existing code-check/design-change sentence to that filter. Either leave that sentence as it is or note it as an existing statement, outside this change.

findings.summary: A loosening answer can name a gate unrelated to the event it introspects.
findings.evidence: apply_answer accepts relax or remove for any gate in the whole-repository counts that has disagreements >= 1. It does not check that the gate had anything to do with the event being introspected. A rejection that the `verifier` gate caused could produce a relax answer for `test`. Fix: When the event has a job that a gate ended, require the named gate to be one of that job's gates. Accept any counted gate only for events with no job, or state in the docs that the event is only the trigger and the evidence is the counts.

findings.summary: Step numbers in the dependents and seams are off by one.
findings.evidence: The dependents list says the status.rs unit test is in "step 5" and the criterion 4 seam says the field is added in step 5 and gate_counts_lines in step 6. In the steps list, status.rs is step 6 and display.rs is step 7. Fix: Renumber the references to match the steps list.

findings.summary: The plan narrows the reading's disagreement signals without saying the records cannot support the others.
findings.evidence: The reading's assumption lists 'a later rerun, the verifier, or an unchanged next-try landing' as disagreement signals, and 'sent back' as an end. JobRecords (store.rs:22-46) has one candidate and one verification per job, so cross-job retries are the only signal recorded. The plan raises this as a user question but does not say that the records hold no within-job rerun. Fix: Add one sentence saying a job record holds one verification, so a within-job rerun or send-back cannot be counted from existing records.
findings.location: Decision 1, rejected alternative 'Also count a later green rerun or verifier pass'

summary: I checked the round-4 plan against the snapshot using Read and Grep. Everything it relies on exists where it says: PreventionKind with ALL and as_str (records.rs:1342-1350), the only exhaustive match on it (status.rs:1707), the Candidate fields base_fingerprint, changes, fingerprint and violations (records.rs:774-787), reading::retried_job, retry_introspection and retry_cause (reading.rs:1413-1525), briefs::class_summaries (briefs.rs:349), cause_key, addressing_request and repeated_causes (hestia.rs:264-388), error_review and try_error_review (hestia.rs:2347-2389), read_records building cases (introspect.rs:388-413), apply_answer and its error text (introspect.rs:1453-1499), SYSTEM_PROMPT and the schema enum (introspect.rs:1006-1042), athena_bin and the scripted Model's prompt capture in the CLI test (introspection.rs:38, 291), and check_durations in display.rs:1199. `known` in introspect() is store::Records (introspect.rs:42), so gate_counts(&known) type-checks. I grepped every reader of prevention_kind, prevention, proposed_request and .introspections. Each reader that could pass relax text to a producer or turn it into a default (retry seed, class summary, cases, cause groups) is filtered and has a test. labeled.rs and evidence_labels only read failure-class labels, and review.rs and display only show the text, so none of them is harmed. Each demonstration calls a real production entry point and would fail without its behavior. Only the model's JSON reply is scripted. The same-change rule is approximate when the base moved, but the plan says so, prefers the exact fingerprint when the bases are equal, and shows the rule in the status label. The two files outside the deliverable list are justified, and Athena has already flagged them. I found only minor issues and nits.
